entries.words: the whole land rising toward one side, gently
entries.reason: Authored: a slope across a whole world is the simplest land that is not flat; it is bounded to the land near the world so a grade never runs on to the horizon.

entries.words: a hill: a rounded rise of the land, round or long, smooth or rough
entries.reason: Authored: hills are what most worlds stand among; one feature with a width, a depth and a roughness makes round hills, long ridges and rough knolls.

licence.content_source: Authored for Exulanica landforms; see the entry reasons

entries.words: a long hollow between higher ground, with a flat floor
entries.reason: Authored: a valley gives a world two sides that rise and a floor a path or a stream can follow.

licence.content_source: Authored for Exulanica landforms; see the entry reasons

entries.words: small, gentle unevenness over all the ground
entries.reason: Authored: real ground is never a plane; a seeded unevenness of a stated size keeps open ground from reading as a floor.

licence.content_source: Authored for Exulanica landforms; see the entry reasons

entries.words: mountains or hills on the horizon, far beyond the world
entries.reason: Authored: a skyline gives a world depth to the horizon; a range is drawn only, never walked, so its heights are not held to the near land's bound.

licence.content_source: Authored for Exulanica landforms; see the entry reasons

entries.words: the land falling to the sea along one side, with a beach
entries.reason: Authored: the sea is the datum every height is measured from; a shore carves the land down to a beach and a sea floor with real depth beyond it.

licence.content_source: Authored for Exulanica landforms; see the entry reasons

entries.words: a bowl in the ground; filled, a lake or a pond
entries.reason: Authored: water needs a bed for its depth to be seen; a basin carves one, and when filled its level is its lowest rim less a freeboard.

licence.content_source: Authored for Exulanica landforms; see the entry reasons

entries.words: steps cut into a slope, each a level bench above the land it covers
entries.reason: Authored: terraced hillsides are how people have long built and farmed on slopes; benches follow the land and fade out at their ends.
